headline: A 2017 law permanently lets Washington, Oregon, and California set their own fishing rules for Dungeness crab in federal waters off their coasts where no federal fishery plan applies.
what_it_does: Before this law, a provision from a 1998 law gave these three states this power only for a limited time. This law removes that end date, so the authority continues. It applies only to Dungeness crab fisheries that have no federal fishery management plan in effect.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial Dungeness crab fishers in Washington, Oregon, and California
who_it_affects.how: State rules on fishing in the federal zone off their coast can continue to apply to them without a planned end date.

who_it_affects.group: Crab processors and seafood businesses in those three states
who_it_affects.how: They are affected by the same state fishing and processing rules that apply to the crab they buy and handle.

who_it_affects.group: State fish and wildlife agencies in Washington, Oregon, and California
who_it_affects.how: They keep the legal power to adopt and enforce crab fishing rules in federal waters where no federal plan exists.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 18, 2017, with the end date removed so the state authority does not expire.
